source_refs.note: Exercise 1.2, Question 4 (book p. 14): pick the non-fundamental transcendental functions; answer key p. 297

blocks.prompt: 4. Which of the following functions are non-fundamental transcendental functions? \(f(x) = e^{2x}\), \(g(x) = \cos x\), \(h(x) = 2^{x}\), \(k(x) = \cos x^{2}\), \(r(x) = 2^{-x}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh Question 3 ka ulta hai: is dafa non-fundamental transcendental functions dhoondne hain.
Diya kya hai? Paanch transcendental functions.
Find kya karna hai? Kaun se non-fundamental hain.
Kaunsa rule? Non-fundamental woh hai jo standard functions ko jor kar ya ek ko doosre ke andar daal kar (composition) banaya gaya ho. Jo exponential ek akele \(a^{x}\) mein badla ja sake (jaise \(e^{2x}\) ya \(2^{-x}\)) woh fundamental hi rehta hai.
Plan: har function ko dobara likh kar dekhenge ke us mein jama, zarb ya composition chhupa hai ya nahin.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = e^{2x}\), \(g(x) = \cos x\), \(h(x) = 2^{x}\), \(k(x) = \cos x^{2}\), \(r(x) = 2^{-x}\).
Maloom karna: non-fundamental transcendental functions.
Tareeqa: har function ko ek akele standard function (\(a^{x}\), \(\ln x\), \(\sin x\), \(\cos x\), \(\sin^{-1} x\), ...) ki shakal mein likhne ki koshish. Jo is tarah na likha ja sake woh non-fundamental hai.

\(f(x) = e^{2x}\)
\[e^{2x} = \left(e^{2}\right)^{x}\]
Fundamental.
Kyun: exponents ke qaide se yeh ek akela exponential \(a^{x}\) hai, \(a = e^{2}\). Question 3 mein bhi yahi dekha tha.

\(g(x) = \cos x\)
Fundamental.
Kyun: yeh standard trigonometric function hai, bilkul \(\sin x\) ki tarah jis ka naam 1.3.1 mein hai.

\(k(x) = \cos x^{2}\)
\[k(x) = \cos\left(x^{2}\right)\]
Non-fundamental.
Kyun: yeh composition hai: pehle algebraic function \(x^{2}\) bana, phir use trigonometric function \(\cos\) ke andar daal diya. Section 1.3.2 kehta hai ke composition se bane functions non-fundamental hote hain.
Dhyan dein: \(\cos x^{2}\) ka matlab \(\cos(x^{2})\) hai, \((\cos x)^{2}\) nahin.

\(r(x) = 2^{-x}\)
\[2^{-x} = \left(2^{-1}\right)^{x} = \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x}\]
Fundamental.
Kyun: minus power dekh kar dhoka na khaiye: yeh ek akela exponential \(a^{x}\) hai, \(a = \frac{1}{2}\), jo \(a > 0\) aur \(a \ne 1\) ki shart poori karta hai.
Tasdeeq: answer key bhi sirf \(k(x) = \cos x^{2}\) batati hai. Jawab mil gaya.
blocks.final_answer: Sirf \(k(x) = \cos x^{2}\) non-fundamental transcendental function hai. (\(f, g, h, r\) fundamental hain.)
